summary:
Implemented the terminal window title setting in the repository, without committing and without running tests, Black, or mypy (verified by reading only).

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 after ERASE_IN_LINE; added Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added the format entry returning "\x1b]0;{title}\x07" and the Control.title(title) classmethod, which passes (SET_WINDOW_TITLE, title) as one two-item argument.
- rich/console.py: added set_window_title beside show_cursor. It checks only is_terminal, buffers the control and returns True, or returns False with nothing written. Google-style docstring includes the required caveats.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: one new elif branch calling term.set_title(title) with the second item. Win32 wrapper unchanged.
- CHANGELOG.md: Unreleased "Added" bullet linking pull request 2200.
- Tests: test_console.py (test_set_window_title, skipped on win32), test_control.py (test_control_title), test_windows_renderer.py (test_control_set_window_title, asserting set_title called once with "Hello, world!").

Choices to review: the Console test skips on sys.platform == "win32" rather than detecting legacy Windows specifically. Added lines were checked to stay under 88 characters, but Black was not run.
